page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Rewrite as 60° ± 18°
steps.margin_note: First mark, and the trick. 42° is 60° − 18° and 78° is 60° + 18°, so the first two are a matched pair around 60°. The third reduces to −cos18°.

recall.must_convey: That 42° and 78° are written as 60° ∓ 18° and 162° as 180° − 18°.
accept: write forty two as sixty minus eighteen and seventy eight as sixty plus eighteen and one sixty two as one eighty minus eighteen
spot that the first two are sixty either side of eighteen
rewrite all three around eighteen degrees
forty two ante sixty minus eighteen, seventy eight ante sixty plus eighteen
express them in terms of eighteen degrees

steps.why: All three angles are built from 18°, and seeing that is the whole question. Without the rewrite there is nothing to combine.
common_mistakes: Trying to evaluate each cosine separately.

steps.label: Apply cos(A+B) + cos(A−B)
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The pair collapses to 2cos60°cos18° = cos18°, which the third term cancels exactly.

recall.must_convey: That the pair becomes 2cos60°cos18° = cos18°, which cancels the third term to give 0.
accept: the pair gives two cos sixty cos eighteen which is cos eighteen and that cancels the last term
two times a half is one so it leaves cos eighteen minus cos eighteen
two cos sixty cos eighteen ante cos eighteen, cancel ayi zero

steps.why: cos60° = 1/2 exactly cancels the 2 in front, leaving a single cos18° — which is precisely what the third term subtracts.
common_mistakes: Using the difference formula and getting sines.
